findings.overview:
Claw Code (ultraworkers/claw-code) is a public, MIT-licensed Rust implementation of the `claw` CLI agent harness. Its own README describes it as an "agent-managed museum exhibit" rather than a production product: it is developed and maintained by other agent harnesses (Gajae-Code / LazyCodex), and users are pointed to those for real work. The stack is a multi-crate Cargo workspace: `api` (provider clients, SSE, request/response types, retry/preflight, prompt cache), `runtime` (`ConversationRuntime`, session persistence, system-prompt assembly, compaction, permissions, hooks, MCP), `tools` (ToolSpec definitions plus execution and file ops), `commands` (slash commands), `plugins`, `telemetry`, `sdk`, `rusty-claude-cli` (the `claw` binary), plus `mock-anthropic-service` and `compat-harness` for parity tests. There is also a Python "porting workspace" in `src/` (QueryEnginePort, tools.py, runtime.py) that mirrors command/tool inventories and session bookkeeping, but it does not call an LLM; it is a reference scaffold, not the runtime.

It is not lean. The CLI `main.rs` is about 19,800 lines / 804 KB, `tools/src/lib.rs` is 11,638 lines / 427 KB, `commands/src/lib.rs` is 263 KB, and the runtime is 47 flat modules. The useful core for our purposes is small and clean: `ApiClient::stream`, `ToolExecutor::execute`, `ConversationRuntime::run_turn`, `SystemPromptBuilder`, and the OpenAI-compatible serializer, which has first-class handling for `deepseek-v4-pro` / `deepseek-v4-flash` (a `thinking` parameter and `reasoning_content` echo).
findings.coreMechanisms:
1) Loop entry is `ConversationRuntime::run_turn` at `rust/crates/runtime/src/conversation.rs:573`. It pushes the user input into `Session.messages`, enters `loop` at :608, and each iteration first checks interruption and `iterations > self.max_iterations` (:609-621). It then builds `ApiRequest { system_prompt: self.system_prompt.clone(), messages: self.session.messages.clone() }` (:623-626) and calls `self.api_client.stream(request)`. The event stream is folded into `ContentBlock`s by `build_assistant_message` (:1084); a missing `MessageStop` or empty block list is a hard error (:1127-1134). The assistant message is appended to the session before any tool runs (:671-674). Auto-compaction is checked immediately after (:678, implementation :922-945). Then `pending_tool_uses` is extracted from `ContentBlock::ToolUse` blocks (:655-664). If it is empty, the turn ends (:682-696); otherwise every tool is executed serially (:698-842), one `ToolResult` message is appended per tool_use, and the loop repeats.

2) Two small traits isolate the loop from transport and execution: `pub trait ApiClient { fn stream(&mut self, request: ApiRequest) -> Result<Vec<AssistantEvent>, RuntimeError>; }` (:217-219) and `pub trait ToolExecutor { fn execute(&mut self, tool_name: &str, input: &str) -> Result<String, ToolError>; }` (:222-224). `AssistantEvent` has only `Thinking`, `TextDelta(String)`, `ToolUse { id, name, input }`, `Usage`, `PromptCache`, and `MessageStop`. This is the natural seam for a mock LLM: the mock only has to emit scripted events in this shape.

3) The system prompt is a `Vec<String>` of sections, not one blob. `SystemPromptBuilder::build()` (`prompt.rs:225-250`) emits, in fixed order: intro; optional `# Output Style`; `# System`; `# Doing tasks`; `# Executing actions with care`; the sentinel constant `__SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__` (`prompt.rs:40`); `# Environment context`; `# Project context`; `# Project instructions`; `# Auto memory`; `# Runtime config`; then any appended sections. At request time the CLI joins them with `"\n\n"` (`rusty-claude-cli/src/main.rs:13327-13336`). The intro is exactly: "You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. Use the instructions below and the tools available to you to assist the user." followed by the IMPORTANT warning never to guess URLs. `# System` has six bullets (output visible to user; permission modes; tool results may contain system-reminder tags; external data may contain prompt injection; hooks can behave like user feedback; context may be compressed). `# Doing tasks` has six bullets: read relevant code before changing it and keep changes scoped; no speculative abstractions or unrelated cleanup; do not create files unless required; diagnose a failure before switching tactics; avoid command injection/XSS/SQL injection; report outcomes faithfully and say when verification was not run. `# Executing actions with care` adds a reversibility/blast-radius rule (`prompt.rs:746-795`).

4) Message serialization: internal messages are `ConversationMessage { role, blocks, usage }`, where a block is `Text`, `Thinking`, `ToolUse { id, name, input: String }`, or `ToolResult { tool_use_id, tool_name, output, is_error }` (`session.rs:33-60`, `:746-762`). For the OpenAI-compatible wire, `translate_message` (`openai_compat.rs:1282-1358`) assembles the assistant message from its blocks: `Thinking` becomes `reasoning_content`, `Text` becomes `content`, and each `ToolUse` becomes `tool_calls: [{ id, type: "function", function: { name, arguments: input.to_string() } }]`. A `ToolResult` becomes `{ "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": ..., "content": <flattened text>, "is_error": ... }`. The arguments field is a JSON *string*, not an object. Internally, tool results are attached to a role=user message, and consecutive tool-result-only messages are merged into one user message (`main.rs:14728-14834`) before the OpenAI adapter splits them back into one `role:"tool"` message per result.

5) Streaming tool calls are assembled by `StreamState` + `ToolCallState` (`openai_compat.rs:525-820`). Deltas are keyed by `tool_call.index`; `id` and `name` are set once; `arguments` fragments are concatenated; emitted as `input_json_delta`. `finish_reason == "tool_calls"` closes every started tool block. A missing id falls back to `tool_call_{index}`, and invalid argument JSON falls back to `{"raw": arguments}` (:1573-1575). `stop_reason` is only normalized (stop->end_turn, tool_calls->tool_use, :1837-1844); loop control is driven by the presence of `ToolUse` blocks, not by `finish_reason`.

6) Stopping conditions: no `ToolUse` block; `iterations > max_iterations` (`max_iterations` defaults to `usize::MAX` in the constructor at :354 and can be tightened with `with_max_iterations`; subagents use `DEFAULT_AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 32` at `tools/src/lib.rs:4257-4259`); user interruption via `TurnInterruptSignal`; or a turn-control abort. There is no explicit "task complete" tool: a model message with no tool calls ends the turn. On interruption or permission denial, every pending tool_use still receives a synthesized `tool_result` with `is_error=true`, so the next request has a valid transcript (:704-722, :770-778).

7) Provider tuning nuance: `is_reasoning_model` (`openai_compat.rs:972-986`) only matches o1/o3/o4/grok-3-mini/qwq/*-thinking; `deepseek-v4` is not in that list, so V4 requests do not automatically strip temperature/top_p. DeepSeek V4 is handled separately by the reasoning-history logic below.
findings.toolUse:
Tool definitions live in `mvp_tool_specs() -> Vec<ToolSpec>` at `rust/crates/tools/src/lib.rs:484`, with 57 ToolSpec entries: `bash`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `glob_search`, `grep_search`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `TodoWrite`, `Skill`, `Agent`, `ToolSearch`, `NotebookEdit`, `Sleep`, `SendUserMessage`, `Config`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`, `StructuredOutput`, `REPL`, `PowerShell`, `AskUserQuestion`, `TaskCreate/RunTaskPacket/TaskGet/TaskList/TaskStop/TaskUpdate/TaskOutput`, the `Worker*` family, `TeamCreate/Delete`, `CronCreate/Delete/List`, `MemoryRead/Write`, `LSP`, the MCP family, `RemoteTrigger`, `TestingPermission`, and `GitStatus/Diff/Log/Show/Blame`. Each is `ToolSpec { name, description, input_schema, required_permission }`.

The core six schemas (verbatim structure):
- `bash`: required `["command"]`; optional `timeout` (integer, min 1), `description`, `run_in_background`, `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`, `namespaceRestrictions`, `isolateNetwork`, `filesystemMode` enum `["off","workspace-only","allow-list"]`, `allowedMounts` (array of strings).
- `read_file`: required `["path"]`; optional `offset` (min 0), `limit` (min 1).
- `write_file`: required `["path","content"]`.
- `edit_file`: required `["path","old_string","new_string"]`; optional `replace_all` (boolean).
- `glob_search`: required `["pattern"]`; optional `path`.
- `grep_search`: required `["pattern"]`; optional `path`, `glob`, `output_mode`, `-B`, `-A`, `-C`, `context`, `-n`, `-i`, `type`, `head_limit`, `offset`, `multiline`.
All six end with `"additionalProperties": false`.

On the wire, `openai_tool_definition` (`openai_compat.rs:1493-1504`) emits `{"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters"}}`; `normalize_object_schema` (:1468-1491) recursively adds `"properties": {}` and `"additionalProperties": false` to every object node so strict OpenAI-compatible backends accept the schema. `tool_choice` maps `Auto -> "auto"`, `Any -> "required"`, `Tool{name} -> {"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` (:1506-1515).

Execution is `execute_tool_with_enforcer` (`tools/src/lib.rs:1396-1529`): an exact-name match; an unknown name returns `Err("unsupported tool: {name}")`. Before dispatch, a permission check uses `PermissionMode::{ReadOnly, WorkspaceWrite, DangerFullAccess}`. bash/PowerShell are classified by the command text; read/write/edit/glob/grep by whether the path is inside the workspace. A denial becomes a `tool_result` with `is_error=true`, not a loop abort. `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` hooks can rewrite input, deny or cancel a call, and append feedback to the output (`conversation.rs:724-833`).

All tool outputs are serialized with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` (`tools/src/lib.rs:2884`). `read_file` returns `{type:"text", file:{filePath, content, numLines, startLine, totalLines}, truncationFooter?}` (`file_ops.rs:149-170`). `write_file` returns `{type:"create"|"update", filePath, content, structuredPatch, originalFile, gitDiff}` (:186-200) and automatically calls `create_dir_all(parent)` (:639-644). `edit_file` returns `{filePath, oldString, newString, originalFile, structuredPatch, userModified, replaceAll, gitDiff}` (:202-221) and errors when `old_string == new_string` or `old_string` is absent (:669-680). Reads and writes are capped at 10 MB (`file_ops.rs:16-19`). bash stdout/stderr are truncated to 16,384 bytes with the marker `[output truncated — exceeded 16384 bytes]` (`bash.rs:485-499`).

For streaming, the SSE parser splits on blank lines (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`), ignores `[DONE]`, detects raw JSON error objects and HTML responses (with the hint "check endpoint URL") instead of failing on a deserialize error (`openai_compat.rs:1577-1713`). The endpoint builder is `base_url.trim_end_matches('/') + "/chat/completions"` unless the base already ends with that suffix (:1739-1746).
findings.contextManagement:
The system prompt has four layers: static behavior sections (intro, System, Doing tasks, Executing actions with care); dynamic environment (model family, model, working directory, date, platform); project context (git status, last five commits, git diff, discovered instruction files); and optional memory plus runtime-config JSON. Hard caps are `MAX_INSTRUCTION_FILE_CHARS = 4_000`, `MAX_TOTAL_INSTRUCTION_CHARS = 12_000`, and `MAX_GIT_DIFF_CHARS = 50_000`; oversize content is truncated with a marker (`prompt.rs:41-43`). Instruction discovery walks from cwd up to the git root, checking in each directory `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAW.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claw/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claw/instructions.md`, then `.claw/rules`, `.claw/rules.local` and framework imports; duplicate content is removed by hash (`prompt.rs:345-369`).

History is not trimmed per turn: every API call sends the full `session.messages`. Compaction is in `compact.rs`: defaults are `preserve_recent_messages: 4` and `max_estimated_tokens: 10_000` (:16-22). When the compactable portion has more than four messages and its estimated token count is at least 10k, older messages are summarized into one synthetic internal `System` message, the most recent four are preserved verbatim, and any previous summary is merged. The continuation text is exactly: "This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation." plus "Recent messages are preserved verbatim." plus "Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, and do not preface with continuation text." (`compact.rs:3-6`). The compaction boundary is explicitly walked back so an assistant ToolUse / tool_result pair is never split (:123-166).

Automatic compaction fires when cumulative `input_tokens >= 100_000` (`conversation.rs:22-23`), overridable with the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_INPUT_TOKENS`; the threshold can be lowered at runtime after a context-window 400 (`set_auto_compaction_input_tokens_threshold`). Token estimates are `chars / 4 + 1` per block (`compact.rs:458-473`). Before a request, the serialized payload is estimated at `bytes / 4` and `input estimate + max_tokens` is compared with the model context window (`providers/mod.rs:706-737`). `max_tokens_for_model` returns 64,000 by default and 32,000 for opus (`providers/mod.rs:623-633`).

There is also a 30-second-TTL completion cache keyed by a request fingerprint and prompt-cache usage accounting (`prompt_cache.rs:10-16`), and session persistence to JSONL redacts secrets and truncates any field to 16 KB (`session.rs:15-17`). The CLI rebuilds the runtime from the persisted session at the start of each `run_turn` (`main.rs:8020-8051`), so session state, not process memory, is the source of truth.
findings.errorHandling:
1) HTTP retries: `send_with_retry` (`openai_compat.rs:312-346`) makes up to 8 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1 s and capped at 128 s, plus additive jitter; a 429 honors `Retry-After`. Retryable statuses are 408, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, and 529 (:1801-1806). A 400 whose body contains "no parseable body", "connection reset", "broken pipe", or "empty reply from server" is treated as a gateway flake and retried (:1812-1821). Exhaustion returns `RetriesExhausted`. Status-specific hints exist for 401 (check API key), 403 (permissions), 413 (reduce prompt), 429 (wait), 500 and 502-504 (retry) (:1825-1835).

2) Preflight: request body size limits (OpenAI 100 MB, xAI 50 MB, DashScope 6 MB, :48-51) and context-window validation (`input estimate + max_tokens > window` raises `ContextWindowExceeded`, `providers/mod.rs:706-724`).

3) Post-tool stall: after a tool result, the first stream event has a 10-second `POST_TOOL_STALL_TIMEOUT` (`rusty-claude-cli/src/main.rs:282`). On timeout the stalled connection is dropped and the same request is re-sent once as a continuation nudge; only a second failure is an error (:13345-13372).

4) Tool errors do not kill the turn: a tool `Err(String)` is wrapped into a `tool_result` with `is_error=true` and fed back to the model (`conversation.rs:783-826`). Permission denials, hook denials, and user interruption also produce `is_error=true` tool results (:704-722, :828-833). A stream without `MessageStop` or with no content blocks is a turn-level error (:1127-1134).

5) Loop guard: `iterations > self.max_iterations` returns `RuntimeError("conversation loop exceeded the maximum number of iterations")` (:615-621).

6) Structured recovery: `recovery_recipes.rs` defines `FailureScenario` (trust prompt unresolved, prompt misdelivery, stale branch, compile red cross crate, MCP handshake, partial plugin startup, provider failure), `RecoveryStep`, and `EscalationPolicy::{AlertHuman, LogAndContinue, Abort}`. Every recipe uses `max_attempts: 1`, so one automatic attempt is made and then the failure is escalated (:284-334); a ledger records `attempt_count`, `retry_limit`, `attempts_remaining`, and per-step results (:155-169).

7) After compaction, a session health probe calls `glob_search` with a deliberately non-matching pattern to verify the tool executor is responsive (`conversation.rs:504-518`).

8) Streaming parser errors: a raw JSON error object inside a data frame is surfaced with its message; an HTML response (typically a wrong base URL) is reported as `invalid_response` with the action "verify the API endpoint URL is correct" (`openai_compat.rs:1614-1712`).

lessonsForOurAgent: Copy the two-interface split, not the whole framework: `LLMClient.stream(messages, tools) -> list[Event]` and `ToolExecutor.execute(name, args_json) -> str`. A mock LLM implements the same `stream` method and returns scripted `tool_use`/text events, so steps 3-7 run offline before the real DeepSeek key is wired in.

Use the exact loop order: append the user message, build a request from the full history, append the assistant message, then execute each tool_call and append one tool message per call, then repeat. Do not execute tools before recording the assistant tool_calls.

Every `tool_call.id` must get exactly one matching tool message before the next assistant turn. Errors, denials, skips, and interruptions still need a tool message (`is_error=true` or an `ERROR:` prefix), otherwise DeepSeek returns a 400 for an orphaned tool message.

For `deepseek-v4-pro`, mirror the repo's V4 handling: send `"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}` in the request body; echo prior assistant reasoning back as `reasoning_content`; for an assistant message that contains only tool_calls, omit `content` and send `"reasoning_content": ""`; send `functions[].arguments` as a JSON string, not an object.

Keep tool schemas strict: `type:object`, explicit `properties`, `required`, and `additionalProperties:false`. Six to eight tools are enough (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `list_dir`/`glob`, `grep`, `run_check`/`bash`, optionally `finish`); do not clone the repo's 57 tools.

Make `write_file` create parent directories automatically and return JSON metadata (`path`, `bytes`, `created|updated`, patch summary); make `edit_file` require an exact `old_string`, reject `old_string == new_string`, and report a clear error when the string is missing.
Truncate tool output aggressively (the repo uses 16 KB for bash and 10 MB for file I/O). A single failing check with a huge traceback can otherwise consume the whole context window.

Encode tool failures as tool-result content instead of Python exceptions. The model then sees the error on the next turn and can repair it; this is the repo's main self-healing mechanism. Keep a separate, bounded repair counter for generated-project checks (2-3 rounds, then emit the project with a warning).

Set an explicit loop cap (30-60 iterations) instead of copying the repo's `usize::MAX` default. Also cap each individual tool's runtime (the repo uses a `timeout` tool parameter and kills the process on expiry).

Do not trust a model's claim of completion: treat 'no tool_calls' as the end of the turn, then run independent completion checks (all planned files exist, `py_compile` passes, JSON is valid, requirements/dependency files are present). A `finish(summary)` tool can provide an explicit signal, but validation should remain external.

Budget tokens with `len(text)/4` and compact when the history reaches roughly 60-70% of the model window. Preserve the last 4-6 messages, summarize older ones into one synthetic continuation message, and never split an assistant tool_calls message from its tool results.

Add retries around the API call: exponential backoff from 1 s up to about 60 s, retry 429/5xx/timeouts, honor `Retry-After`, and preflight payload size. A 400 from a wrong base URL often comes back as HTML; detect that and print 'check endpoint URL' rather than a JSON decode error.

Preprocess the two markdown architecture docs into one JSON manifest (file list, dependencies, acceptance commands, module boundaries) and validate it with dataclasses/JSON Schema before the agent runs. The repo's Python scaffold does the same with `src/tools.py` loading `src/reference_data/tools_snapshot.json` via `lru_cache`; feed the model the manifest, not the raw markdown every turn.

For the Tkinter GUI, mirror `ConversationEvent::{AgentBegin, ToolUse, ToolResult, AgentEnd}` and run the agent in a worker thread that pushes events into a `queue.Queue`; the UI consumes them with `after()`. This keeps the mainloop responsive and gives a natural progress bar for per-file generation.

Do not copy the repo's incidental complexity: hooks, MCP, plugins, a permission enforcer, prompt caching, multi-provider routing, and 57 tools are not needed for this assignment. Keep workspace containment, simple path validation, write permission, and a small tool set.

findings.overview:
This repository is an educational, unofficial architecture analysis of Claude Code, published as a Docsify documentation site (index.html, _sidebar.md, Markdown chapters, Mermaid diagrams) with 21 chapters in parallel Chinese and English trees. It is not an implementation: it analyzes a community-circulated snapshot of roughly 512,000 lines / 1,884 TypeScript files (about v2.1.6x, late March 2026) and carries an explicit disclaimer that it is independent research, not Anthropic's official design, and redistributes no Anthropic source. Its companion project, Windy3f3f3f3f/claude-code-from-scratch (2,821 stars, Python as primary language), is a clean-room reimplementation of about 4,300 lines across TypeScript and Python, with a 13-chapter tutorial; its Python package mini_claude contains agent.py, tools.py, prompt.py, context.py, and a ~1,300-line, 6-file, 6-tool canonical version under steps/canonical/py.

The analysis's stack is therefore TypeScript (Bun, React/Ink, Zod, MCP) for the studied system, Markdown/Docsify for the book, and Python 3.11+ with the anthropic, openai, and rich packages for the companion implementation. The most useful parts for our project are chapter 2 (main loop), chapter 3 (context engineering), chapter 4 (tool system), chapter 5 (editing strategy), chapter 13/15 (minimal necessary components), and the companion's canonical Python agent, which contains a directly copyable while-loop and OpenAI-compatible message conversion.
findings.coreMechanisms:
The architecture is a two-layer async-generator design. QueryEngine.ts (~1,295 lines) is the session layer: submitMessage() runs 8 phases (setup, orphaned-permission replay, processUserInput, system-init message, local-command early return, main query loop, budget check, result extraction) and owns persistence, cost, permissions, and cancellation. query.ts (~1,728 lines) is the per-cycle state machine. Each iteration runs a compression pass (applyToolResultBudget, history snip, microcompact, context collapse, autocompact), builds the request (system prompt + tool schemas + messages), streams callModel(), collects the assistant message and tool_use blocks, executes tools via runTools(), injects attachments, then decides continue or terminate. The loop is an async function* that yields stream events, so the caller renders tokens as they arrive; mutable cross-iteration state is a single State object reassigned at each continue site.

Stopping conditions: (1) the model returns no tool_use blocks — plain text means done, with no special "finished" token or counter; (2) maxTurns reached; (3) USD budget exceeded (getTotalCost() >= maxBudgetUsd); (4) abortController signal (user interrupt); (5) unrecoverable error after all prompt-too-long/max-output recovery fails. Seven explicit continue sites encode recovery: next_turn (normal tool call), collapse_drain_retry and reactive_compact_retry (PTL recovery), max_output_tokens_escalate (raise to 64K), max_output_tokens_recovery (inject a continuation user message, up to 3 times), stop_hook_blocking (a stop hook refuses termination), and token_budget_continuation.

The minimal implementation is deliberately smaller: a 65-line chatAnthropic() while(true) appends the user message, calls the model (optionally streaming), appends the full assistant content, extracts tool_use blocks, breaks if there are none, executes each tool, appends all tool_result blocks as one user message, then calls checkAndCompact(). Chapter 15 distills seven essential components: prompt orchestration, tool registry, agent loop, file operations, shell execution, edit strategy, and CLI UX. Its phased roadmap is ~500 lines with read_file/write_file/run_shell, ~2,000 lines adding permission confirmation, edit_file, grep/list, and session persistence, ~5,000 lines adding streaming, auto-compaction, retries, and cost display, and ~20,000 lines adding the multi-level compression pipeline, AST security, MCP, and multi-agent.

A second, post-snapshot mechanism is the /goal autonomy loop: a session-scoped Stop hook sends the condition plus transcript to a separate judge model with no tools; the judge returns JSON {ok, reason, impossible}; "no" re-prompts the main model with the reason; "impossible" is a deliberate loop brake. The companion Python version implements pursue_goal() as at most 5 evaluator rounds before giving up.
findings.toolUse:
Every tool implements one Tool interface: name, aliases, maxResultSizeChars, shouldDefer, call(args, context, canUseTool, onProgress), description()/prompt(), Zod inputSchema plus optional JSON Schema, isConcurrencySafe(), isReadOnly(), isDestructive(), validateInput(), checkPermissions(), and React render methods. buildTool() supplies fail-closed defaults: isConcurrencySafe false, isReadOnly false, checkPermissions allow. Tools are assembled in three layers: getAllBaseTools() (static imports plus feature-gated require(), compile-time dead-code elimination), getTools() (SIMPLE mode keeps only Bash/Read/Edit; REPL filtering; deny-rule filtering; isEnabled()), and assembleToolPool() (built-ins sorted as a contiguous prefix, MCP tools sorted as a suffix, uniqBy name so built-ins win). The partitioned sort exists to preserve a cache breakpoint after the last built-in tool.

Execution is an 8-stage pipeline shared by built-in, MCP, and REPL tools: lookup by name/alias, two-phase validation (Zod safeParse/coercion then business validateInput), parallel launch of PreToolUse hook and Bash classifier, chained permission check (hook allow/deny first, then tool checkPermissions, then rules from 8 sources with deny > ask > allow, then speculative classifier, then interactive Allow once/Always allow/Deny), tool.call() with onProgress, result mapping and large-result persistence, PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure hooks, and emission of a tool_result block. Errors never crash the loop: schema failures are wrapped in <\tool_use_error> XML, validation errors carry an errorCode, runtime exceptions are caught, and everything becomes a tool_result with is_error: true so the model can self-correct.

Serialization in the Anthropic format is: assistant message content contains tool_use blocks {type:"tool_use", id, name, input}; the next user message content contains matching tool_result blocks {type:"tool_result", tool_use_id, content, is_error?}. The companion's OpenAI-compatible path converts definitions to {"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters": schema}} and serializes an assistant message with a tool_calls array of {id, type:"function", function:{name, arguments: JSON string}}, followed by one {"role":"tool","tool_call_id": id, "content": result} message per call. It appends a tool message even when a call was denied or the budget was exceeded, because every tool_call must have a matching response or the provider returns a 400. Streaming tool calls are reassembled by index: id/name arrive once, and function.arguments fragments are concatenated until finish_reason.

Concurrency is declarative: partitionToolCalls() groups consecutive isConcurrencySafe calls into one parallel batch and starts a new serial batch at the first unsafe call; file reads/searches are safe, writes and shell are not. StreamingToolExecutor (530 lines) dispatches a tool as soon as its tool_use JSON block finishes parsing during streaming and tracks queued -> executing -> completed -> yielded. A Bash failure aborts sibling tools via siblingAbortController. Large results are persisted to disk (default 50,000-character threshold via maxResultSizeChars; README mentions 100K for some paths) and replaced with a <\persisted-output> preview of the first 2 KB. The minimal Python implementation instead truncates at 50,000 characters, keeping the first and last halves. Unknown tool names return a string such as "Unknown tool: X" rather than raising.
findings.contextManagement:
Each request has three parts: the system prompt (identity, behavior, tool guidance), system/user context (git branch/status/log computed once per session, CLAUDE.md discovered up the directory tree, current date), and the message history. The system prompt is assembled at runtime, not stored as one constant: seven static sections (Intro, System, Doing Tasks, Actions, Using Your Tools, Tone and Style, Output Efficiency) sit before the sentinel __SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__ and are globally cacheable; dynamic sections (session guidance, memory, environment, language, output style, MCP instructions, scratchpad) come after it. Tool schemas are in the tools[] array, not the system prompt. CLAUDE.md and date are placed in the first user message as a <\system-reminder>, and memory/skill/MCP deltas are injected as attachment messages, so the cached system prefix stays byte-identical.

History growth is controlled by a progressive compression pipeline. Counting conventions differ across chapters: README calls it 4 levels (Snip -> Deduplicate/Microcompact -> Context Collapse -> Summarize), while chapter 3 documents 5 stages by adding Tool Result Budget first. The order is cheapest-first: persist/truncate oversized tool results with no API call; snip old history; microcompact old tool results (time-based when the cache is cold, cache_edits blocks when hot); context-collapse into a reversible projection without modifying originals; autocompact as the last resort. Autocompact forks a sub-agent to summarize. Threshold formulas: reservedTokensForSummary = min(model max output, 20,000); effectiveWindow = contextWindow - reserved; autoCompactThreshold = effectiveWindow - 13,000. For a 200K window this is 179K (~89.5%) or 167K (~83.5%) depending on output reservation. The minimal version uses a simpler 85% trigger.

Token counting avoids extra API calls by anchoring on the most recent API usage record and roughly estimating only newer messages (about chars/4; chars/2 for dense JSON). The result is typically within 5% instead of 30%+. After autocompact, runPostCompactCleanup() restores the 5 most recently read files (each <=5K tokens), reactivates skills (<=25K tokens), resets collapse state, and re-announces lazy tools/agent lists. The summary prompt uses a two-phase analysis-summary pattern: a NO_TOOLS_PREAMBLE ("CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY. Do NOT call any tools."), an <analysis> scratchpad, then a <summary> with nine sections (Primary Request, Key Technical Concepts, Files and Code, Errors and Fixes, Problem Solving, All User Messages, Pending Tasks, Current Work, Optional Next Step). Only the summary is kept; the analysis block is stripped.

The minimal Python compaction is the same idea in miniature: at more than 6 messages, keep the last 2, summarize the older messages with a separate model call, replace history with a synthetic summary user message plus the recent messages, preserving the current task. The full Python implementation adds 4 tiers with constants SNIPPABLE_TOOLS, SNIP_THRESHOLD=0.60, SNIP_HOT_OVERRIDE=0.75, MICROCOMPACT_IDLE_S=300, KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS=3.
findings.errorHandling:
Recoverable errors are withheld from the caller. When query() receives prompt_too_long, it first drains pending context collapses and retries (collapse_drain_retry); if that frees too little, it forces reactive full compaction and retries (reactive_compact_retry); only if both fail does it yield a prompt_too_long error. For max_output_tokens, it first retries at ESCALATED_MAX_TOKENS 64K without injecting a message; if escalation is unavailable or already used, it injects the exact continuation prompt "Output token limit hit. Resume directly — no apology, no recap of what you were doing. Pick up mid-thought if that is where the cut happened. Break remaining work into smaller pieces." and retries up to 3 times. The error message is retained internally but not yielded if recovery succeeds, so the GUI/SDK never sees the intermediate failure.

Retries use exponential backoff with random jitter: delay = min(1000 * 2^attempt, 30000) + random 0-1000 ms, max 3 retries. Only transient statuses 429, 503, and 529 (and network errors such as ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT) are retryable; 400 and 401 are not. The companion Python mirrors this with _is_retryable() and _with_retry().

Tool errors are data, not exceptions: any pipeline stage converts failure into a tool_result (is_error true) that the model can read and act on. Permission denial returns a normal tool result such as "User denied this action." rather than aborting, so the model can choose another approach. normalizeMessagesForAPI() repairs message-list corruption before every request: it merges split assistant messages with the same message.id, strips unsupported thinking/signature/media/tool_reference blocks, and synthesizes missing tool_results or tool_uses so every pair is complete. DenialTrackingState detects repeated denials and injects guidance to stop the model from re-requesting the same blocked action.

Loop-level brakes: maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, abortController, and MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AUTOCOMPACT_FAILURES = 3. After 3 consecutive compaction failures, compaction becomes a no-op for the session rather than retrying forever; source comments cite production data of 1,279 sessions with 50+ consecutive failures and ~250K wasted API calls/day. Security is a separate 7-layer system: workspace trust, permission modes, rule matching (deny > ask > allow across 8 sources), tree-sitter Bash AST analysis with 23 checks (instead of regex), per-tool validation, OS sandbox plus Git worktree isolation, and a final user-confirmation dialog with 200 ms debounce.

The /goal judge is the model-based stopping mechanism: it receives the condition and transcript, has an empty tools array, runs at high reasoning effort, and must emit JSON matching {ok, reason, impossible} enforced by output schema. Its prompt says the assistant claiming impossibility is evidence, not proof, and that slow progress is not impossibility; when unsure it must return {"ok": false} without "impossible". The Python tutorial caps this at 5 rounds and then gives up, which is a good model for bounded auto-repair.
keyImplementationDetails: Primary loop shape (companion steps/canonical/py/agent.py): append user message; while True: optionally compact; build system+tools+messages; call model; append assistant reply; extract tool_use blocks; if none, return; execute each; append one user message containing all tool_result blocks.

Minimal tool set and schemas are plain JSON: read_file(file_path), write_file(file_path, content), edit_file(file_path, old_string, new_string), list_files(pattern, path?), grep_search(pattern, path?), run_shell(command). Tool descriptions explicitly say old_string must match exactly and be unique.

edit_file uniqueness check: count = content.count(old_string); count == 0 -> "Error: old_string not found in {path}"; count > 1 -> "Error: old_string found {count} times in {path}. Must be unique."; otherwise content.replace and write. Production error text: "Found N matches of the string to replace, but replace_all is false."
read_file returns line-numbered content using the format f"{i + 1:4d} | {line}" so the model can anchor edits; write_file calls os.makedirs(dirname, exist_ok=True) before writing.

run_shell uses subprocess with shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30; on nonzero exit it returns "Command failed (exit {code})\nStdout: ...\nStderr: ...". The TypeScript version uses maxBuffer 5 MB and timeout 30,000 ms.

Result truncation constant MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 50000; when exceeded, keep (MAX_RESULT_CHARS-60)/2 characters from each end and insert "[... truncated N chars ...]". list_files caps at 200 paths; grep_search caps at 100 matching lines.

Tool description for FileEditTool contains the hard rule: "You MUST use your Read tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file." The implementation enforces it via a readFileState cache keyed by absolute path.

readFileState entries store content, mtime timestamp, offset/limit, and isPartialView; before an edit, a newer mtime than the cached timestamp triggers a warning/re-read, with a content comparison fallback on Windows because OneDrive/antivirus can change mtime without changing content.

Static system prompt identity: "You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. Use the instructions below and the tools available to you to assist the user." Behavioral bullets include "In general, do not propose changes to code you haven't read" and "Generally prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one."

Tool-use prompt section begins "Do NOT use the Bash to run commands when a relevant dedicated tool is provided" and maps read/edit/create/search operations to Read, Edit, Write, Glob, and Grep. Output-efficiency section: "Go straight to the point. Try the simplest approach first without going in circles. Do not overdo it. Be extra concise."

System prompt cache boundary sentinel is __SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__ (src/constants/prompts.ts:114); seven static sections precede it and are cached with scope global, dynamic sections follow it. Tool schemas are cached with the system breakpoint and should not be reordered between turns.

Compaction constants: AUTOCOMPACT_BUFFER_TOKENS = 13000; MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_FOR_SUMMARY = 20000; DEFAULT_MAX_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS = 50000; PREVIEW_SIZE_BYTES = 2000; POST_COMPACT_MAX_FILES_TO_RESTORE = 5; POST_COMPACT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_FILE = 5000; POST_COMPACT_SKILLS_TOKEN_BUDGET = 25000; MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AUTOCOMPACT_FAILURES = 3.

Minimal auto-compaction trigger: this.lastInputTokenCount > this.effectiveWindow * 0.85; summarize all but the last user message with max_tokens 2048 and system "You are a conversation summarizer. Be concise but preserve important details.", then replace history with a summary user message, a synthetic assistant acknowledgment, and the preserved last user message.

OpenAI-compatible conversion in python/mini_claude/agent.py: _to_openai_tools emits {"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters"}}; requests use chat.completions.create(model, max_tokens=16384, tools=..., messages=..., stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}); tool-call deltas are merged by tc.index and arguments strings concatenated.

Retry policy in both implementations: retryable statuses 429/503/529 plus overloaded/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT; max 3 retries; delay = min(1000 * 2^attempt, 30000) ms plus up to 1000 ms random jitter; abort signals are never retried.

Goal evaluator prompt demands JSON only, one of {"ok": true, "reason": "quote evidence..."}, {"ok": false, "reason": "quote what is missing..."}, or {"ok": false, "impossible": true, "reason": "explain why..."}; it has no tools and uses output_config JSON schema so the verdict cannot exceed that shape. The Python pursue_goal caps evaluation at 5 iterations.
lessonsForOurAgent: Make the loop the core and keep it tiny and explicit. Use one while True in a worker thread with a stop_reason enum: no tool_calls -> completed; turn_count >= max_turns -> max_turns; token/API budget exceeded -> budget; cancel event -> aborted; unrecoverable API error -> error. This mirrors the source's "no tool_use blocks means done" rule and avoids needing a special DONE token.

Serialize DeepSeek/OpenAI-compatible messages exactly: assistant message with content plus tool_calls [{id, type:'function', function:{name, arguments:<JSON string>}}], then one role='tool' message per tool_call_id in the same order. Always emit a tool message even for denied, skipped, unknown, or budget-blocked calls; an unanswered tool_call causes a 400. Parse arguments with json.loads inside try/except and return an error result for malformed JSON.

Keep tool definitions flat and data-driven for 6-8 tools: read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files/grep, create_directory, run_check, and a batch write_files. The source's minimal version deliberately uses JSON objects plus if/elif dispatch instead of a class hierarchy; adopt that until tool count or per-tool behavior demands an interface. A batch write_files tool directly addresses our API-call-cost problem.

Never let execute_tool raise. Catch every exception and return a human-readable "Error: ..." string, return "Unknown tool: X" for hallucinated names, and include exit code, stdout, and stderr for shell failures. The model then self-corrects on the next turn, which is the source's dominant repair mechanism.

Truncate every tool result before it enters history: 50,000 characters total, keeping the head and tail, with an explicit truncation marker; cap grep at ~100 lines and listings at ~200 entries. Optionally persist the full result to a file and return a preview plus path, as production Claude Code does. This single guard prevents most context blowups.

Build the system prompt as static core plus dynamic environment. Static: role, generation rules, read-before-edit, prefer edit over full rewrite, dedicated tools over shell, completion checklist, concise output, no scope creep. Dynamic: output directory, OS, date, the structured JSON derived from the two markdown docs, target file manifest, and current phase. Put the static part first and keep it byte-identical across calls so DeepSeek prefix caching can hit.

For generation, prefer write_file for new files and reserve edit_file for repairs. Copy the source's exact-match uniqueness rule and error text so the model gets actionable feedback. Add create_directory or let write_file auto-create parent directories. For repairs, read the file with line numbers before editing and reject edits to files not read in this session.

Sandbox every path under the chosen output root: resolve the real path, reject absolute paths and '..' escapes, and refuse writes outside the workspace. Keep a regex blocklist for shell commands (rm, sudo, mkfs, dd, shutdown, git push/reset/clean) and run checks with a 30 s timeout and 5 MB output cap. In a GUI app, use an allow-all-within-sandbox mode plus explicit confirmation for anything outside it.

Budget the run, not just each call: track prompt/completion tokens from the API usage field, enforce max_turns (e.g., 40) and a token ceiling, and emit progress events after each tool call. Generate small files in batches (one write_files call containing several files) and show a determinate progress bar based on the file manifest, rather than one API call per file.

Implement auto-repair as a bounded deterministic gate, not an open-ended agent. After each generation phase run py_compile on .py files, json.loads on .json files, and check the required-file manifest; build a structured failure list and send it back as one user message. Allow at most 2-3 repair rounds, add a circuit breaker after 3 consecutive failed rounds, then stop and report unresolved items explicitly. This is the source's tool-error-as-data loop plus its MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AUTOCOMPACT_FAILURES=3 brake, adapted to project generation.

Use an independent completion judge for the "project complete" condition, optionally with a cheap model call returning JSON {ok, reason, impossible}. The judge must see the actual file manifest and check output, not just the generator's claim; enforce the JSON shape; cap rounds (the source's Python goal loop uses 5) and treat "impossible" as a brake requiring concrete evidence. Combine it with deterministic checks so the judge cannot be talked into accepting a broken project.

Manage context with cheap steps first: estimate tokens as characters/4 anchored to the latest API usage; when above ~80-85%, first replace old tool results with placeholders, then summarize older messages into a fixed nine-section summary; keep the last user message, the spec JSON, and a list of recently written/edited files. After compaction, re-inject the 5 most recently touched files (each capped) and the file manifest so the agent does not forget what it just built.

Run the agent off the Tkinter main thread. The worker pushes structured events (assistant text delta, tool_start, tool_result, phase, progress, error, done) into a queue.Queue; the Tk root polls with after(100, ...). Use threading.Event for cancel and check it at the top of the loop and between tool calls. Never touch widgets from the worker thread.

For PyInstaller, keep prompt templates as Python string constants or ship them with --add-data, avoid dynamic imports and runtime file paths relative to __file__, build inside a venv containing only requests/openai and pyinstaller, and test the frozen exe from a clean directory with a fresh output folder. The source's static/dynamic prompt split makes the prompt easy to embed as constants without losing cache stability.
